purpose: Baricitinib is used to treat moderate to severe rheumatoid arthritis in adults when other medications have not worked well enough. It is also approved to treat severe alopecia areata, a condition that causes significant hair loss. In some cases, it has been used to treat COVID-19 in hospitalized patients who need extra oxygen support.
how_it_works: Your immune system sometimes overreacts and causes inflammation that damages your joints or other parts of your body. Baricitinib works by blocking certain proteins inside your cells called JAK enzymes, which act like switches that turn on inflammation. By blocking these switches, the medication helps calm down your overactive immune system and reduce pain, swelling, and damage.
common_side_effects: Upper respiratory infections like the common cold, urinary tract infections, nausea, headache, high cholesterol levels, and cold sores. Some people may also notice their blood cell counts change, so your doctor will do regular blood tests to keep an eye on this.
warnings: This medication can lower your immune system, which means you may be more likely to get serious infections including tuberculosis, fungal infections, and viral infections like shingles. There is also a risk of blood clots, serious heart problems, and a small increased risk of certain cancers, including lymphoma. It should not be used during pregnancy. Your doctor will screen you for infections like tuberculosis before starting this medicine, and you should tell your doctor right away if you develop fever, chills, or any signs of infection.
typical_dosing: For rheumatoid arthritis, the usual dose is 2 mg taken by mouth once a day. For alopecia areata, the typical dose is 2 mg once daily, and your doctor may increase it to 4 mg once daily if needed. It can be taken with or without food, and it is best to take it at the same time each day. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on your kidney function or other medications you take.
